env_fixes: diffs/README.md: no authors' file changed; data_cleaned_rep.csv downloaded with ?format=original; ltm, coefplot, sjPlot, mediation (CRAN source, per-run library, Ncpus=1) installed because they were absent and had no Debian binary candidate; objects saved with save() after source() for extraction.
class_reason: T1 to T5 (all Table 3 coefficients) match the paper to 3 decimals with the same signs and significance buckets, but T6 fails its pre-registered criterion: every Table 3 model uses 4,507 rows (the data have no missing values in any model variable), while the Table 3 note prints N = 4,057; under the strict rules no target set that includes T6 qualifies for A or B. Alternative class on T1 to T5 alone: A. The reproduced N equals the 4,507 the paper itself reports in the abstract, methods, Table 1 and online Tables D1/D2, so this looks like a difference in the printed N only; it does not change any coefficient-based conclusion. Final D needs agent A to see the same.
confidence_reason: Numbers are deterministic and matched by script, but the class turns on how a printed-N-only mismatch (T6) is weighed, which is a judgement for the batch decision.
uncertainties: T6: reproduced N is 4,507 for all five column (1) models and the data have 0 missing values in all 38 model variables (outputs/run_meta.json), so the 4,057 in the Table 3 note cannot arise from listwise deletion in the deposited cleaned data. Whether 4,057 is a typo for 4,507 cannot be confirmed from the materials; the matching coefficients, SEs and R2 to 3 decimals on 4,507 rows are consistent with that reading (inference, not verified).

Class: PROTOCOL section 7 has no category for 'all estimates exact, only a printed N differs'. I proposed D because the pre-registered T6 criterion fails, with A as the alternative on T1 to T5; the batch decision may weigh this differently.

R_c (alternative positive-emotion outcome = standardized mean of Secured and Happiness): coefficient is negative but p is above 0.001, so it does not meet the pre-registered 'negative and p < 0.001' criterion; it is negative and p < 0.05. Robustness does not change the class.
R_b for T1 dropped 0 rows (no |z| > 3 on positive_emo_rv), so its estimate equals the original.
Environment: R 4.5.0 on aarch64 Debian 13 vs the authors' R 4.3.2 on macOS; estimatr 1.0.6 (HC2 default). PCA signs matched online Table C1, so no sign-aligned rerun was needed.
Data preparation script data_preparation_rep.R named in ReadMe.txt is not in the deposit (DATA_STATEMENT.md); the raw-to-cleaned step was not reproduced. Targets use only the deposited cleaned file.

The mediation block (Figure 3) ran to completion without a seed; its outputs were saved in outputs/session_models.RData (object results) but not compared to the paper, since no target depends on them.

PCA loadings vs online Table C1 (outputs/pca_loadings.csv): Comp.1 Sadness: 0.400 (Table C1 0.4); Comp.2 Happiness: -0.659 (Table C1 -0.659); Comp.2 Secured: -0.586 (Table C1 -0.586); Comp.3 Curiosity: -0.635 (Table C1 -0.635); Comp.3 Surprised: -0.558 (Table C1 -0.558). No sign flips, so no sign-aligned rerun was needed.

Context (not a target): Table 3 column (1) R2 from outputs/targets_extracted.csv: positive_emo_rv: reproduced 0.1000 vs paper 0.1; negative_emo: reproduced 0.1312 vs paper 0.131; general_attitude_fic: reproduced 0.2881 vs paper 0.288; general_attitude_real: reproduced 0.4002 vs paper 0.4. All four R2 values round to the paper's three decimals although the reproduced models use 4507 rows.
